newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling pullback seen limited to $1.6270.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling pullback seen limited to $1.6270.

text.p: Sterling stepped back from late Tuesday's and overnight levels above $1.63 but analysts said a further pullback today would find initial support at the intraday low of $1.6270.
A break below here is then expected to find a prop at congestion around the $1.6250-60 area before finding a firmer base at $1.6200.
The $1.62 level, a psychological support just below the pound's recent lows, also coincides with a rising trendline/triangle bottom drawn from the mid-March low of $1.5850.
Though well-supported, cable also faces tough resistance on the upside with trendline resistance/triangle top limiting near-term gains.

"In the bigger picture, it is still ranging and should struggle at the $1.6340 trendline resistance," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America in London. "A move above there would open $1.64 then $1.6540."
As well as being psychological resistance, the $1.64 level also comes in just above last week's top at $1.6395 while the $1.6540-50 area is the early April peak.
Sterling/mark was also keeping to fairly tight ranges, capped on the upside by the round figure and Monday's top of 2.82 marks.

Above here, the 4-1/2 year high of 2.8231 seen in mid-April limits gains but a move higher finds little in its way until the previous range bottom around 2.8280 which held before sterling's plummet in August-September 1992.
Sterling/downside is seen held initially at 2.81 marks, round-figure support and congestion area, before giving way to 2.80 marks, a rising trendline from the mid-March lows.
